findings.reason: the plan must either retire `push`/`active_sprint_id` to match its derived-pointer design or drop the "ceases to be an operation" claim; leaving a stale second owner in place is the defect the plan exists to eliminate.
findings.text: the design states the sprint pointer is derived and "starting a sprint ceases to be an operation at all", but a second persisted owner survives: `active_sprint_id` maintained in `reckon/_store.py:2562-2583` and written by `push_sprint` (project_state.py:2143), still exposed as the live MCP `push` op (mcp.py:1716); the reckon index currently carries `active_sprint_id: "S17"` while the only sprint stored `active` is `S5`, a stale persisted pointer of exactly the class this plan removes

findings.reason: the design should place the whole blocking assembly in `reckon/lifecycle.py` so the three consumers share one owner instead of three assemblies that drift silently.
findings.text: the "derivation wiring" design says an unpassed gate becomes a row in `blocking` "flowing through the existing `effective_status` path" (one path), but three consumers each re-assemble a blocking list and call `effective_status` themselves: `serve._derive_lifecycle` (serve.py:2173), `mcp_views._blocking` (mcp_views.py:2465) and `roadmap.build_roadmap` (roadmap.py:2813), each also re-deriving the persisted-blocked compatibility guard

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design adds no new module; it plugs a small shared derivation behind the existing `effective_status` seam, following the section-layer convention already used by decisions and followups.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan derives sprint focus but leaves a persisted `active_sprint_id` owner and a live `push` operation standing, and the derived blocking list is assembled independently by three consumers.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched reckon and cites the mechanisms it extends: `effective_status` and the blocking derivation, the decisions/followups parser pattern, audit's staleness thresholds, and the skill it does not re-author.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the skill-enforcement rung is a mechanism swap carrying a stated reason (the rule's wording is owned by `uniform-worker-dispatch`), and the `retire_prose` op is a justified extension rather than a parallel wrapper.
